common_name: Orange Beauty Witch Hazel (Vibrant Orange Fragrant Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Best planted in early spring or fall from a container-grown specimen; avoid disturbing roots once established.

directions: Orange Beauty produces vivid orange-yellow, ribbon-shaped flowers with red-purple bases from mid to late winter on bare branches, opening on mild days and curling shut when temperatures drop to guard against frost damage. Plant in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter winds that can desiccate the flowers. The upright-spreading habit and orange-yellow fall foliage make it a strong dual-season specimen; prune only lightly after flowering to remove crossing or dead wood. Established plants are drought-tolerant and largely untroubled by pests or deer.

common_name: Feuerzauber Witch Hazel (Magic Fire Coppery-Red Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant a container-grown or balled specimen in early spring or fall for best establishment.

directions: Also sold as Magic Fire, Feuerzauber (German for 'fire magic') bears slightly fragrant, coppery-orange flowers suffused with red above a deep purple calyx, opening from midwinter to late winter against bare stems. It matures into a vase-shaped, wide-spreading large shrub with medium green foliage that turns strong orange and red in autumn. Site it in moisture-retentive, humus-rich, neutral to slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade with shelter from cold drying wind, which preserves both flower quality and fall color. Minimal pruning is needed beyond removing damaged or crossing wood immediately after bloom.

common_name: Vesna Witch Hazel (Yellow-Orange Fragrant Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Establish from a container-grown plant in early spring or fall; avoid windy, exposed sites.

directions: Vesna is a large, upright witch hazel prized for very fragrant, twisted yellow-orange petals tinted red at the base, set against a deep claret-red calyx, opening late winter into early spring. It grows into a broadly oval, coarse-branched large shrub or small tree with good red, orange, and yellow fall foliage color. Best grown in an open, sunny to partially shaded position sheltered from strong wind, in well-drained, humus-rich, acid to neutral soil. Because of its eventual size, give Vesna ample room and prune only to shape or remove damaged wood right after flowering finishes.

common_name: Hiltingbury Witch Hazel (Copper-Orange Fragrant Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant a container-grown specimen in early spring or fall in a sheltered, open site.

directions: Raised at Hillier's former Hiltingbury nursery in Hampshire, this large cultivar bears scented, spidery copper-orange to red flowers on bare stems through the winter months, followed by large dark green leaves that turn brilliant orange and red in fall. It performs best in an open, sunny to lightly shaded spot sheltered from exposed or windy conditions, in well-drained, humus-rich, acid to neutral soil. Given its considerable eventual size, allow generous space when siting and limit pruning to removing damaged or crossing wood right after flowering. Propagation is typically by layering or grafting rather than seed, since cultivars do not come true.
